submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the pivot word of a precautionary clause: the item that marks something as to be prevented, avoided or watched out for. It peaks on the negated purpose clause (the 'to' of 'not to VERB', with 'not' itself elevated, and the "'t" of don't/won't), on an avoidance/prevention/refusal predicate (avoid, prevent, stop, refuse, reject, deny, oppose, resist, ignore) standing in a modal, 'want to' or purpose-'to' frame, on recommendation frames ('it is best to', 'the key is to', 'you'll want'), and on the 'for'/'on'/'to' of a look-out phrase ('look for', 'watch out for', 'keep an eye on', 'attend to'); it stays near zero on the same words in episodic statements of completed events ('They prevented the fire', 'He avoided the question'), on bare modality with an ordinary verb ('He must go to the store', 'You should drink more water every day'), and on danger described without any precaution ('The storm destroyed every house on the street'). A weaker second mode (0.3-0.6 of max) fires on the newline that ends a colon-terminated label or heading in formatted text ('Safety Guidelines:\n'), much less on ordinary sentence-final newlines (0.2-0.3 of max).

rival_explanations: Narrow token-identity reading: the pole is a plain unigram detector for 'avoid', 'prevent' and the negator 'to'/'not', so it should fire just as strongly on 'They avoided the road last night' and on 'He told me how to go to the party' as on the modal and negated versions.

Broader directive reading: the pole marks any deontic or instructional clause whatever its polarity, so it should also fire on 'You should drink more water every day', 'He must go to the store' and 'It is important to check the settings', where the measured activation stays at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They prevented the fire from spreading across the yard and the warehouse was saved.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Episodic report of a completed prevention with no precautionary frame, one of the hypothesis's named near-zero cases, though the narrow unigram reading predicts firing on 'prevented'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He avoided the question about the missing receipts during the entire interview on Tuesday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Completed avoidance in a past narrative, the hypothesis's own near-zero case, while the narrow reading predicts firing on 'avoided'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She did not finish the quarterly report because the office printer jammed again.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Plain sentence negation with 'not', which the hypothesis scopes to negated purpose clauses only, but which a unigram negator detector would fire on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He must go to the store before it closes at six this evening.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare modality with an ordinary verb, explicitly predicted near zero by the hypothesis but active for both the unigram-'to' and directive rivals.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You should drink more water every day, especially during the hot summer months.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Deontic 'should' with no precaution, purpose 'to' or negator, the hypothesis's named negative and the directive rival's named false positive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We drove to the coast and back before the children woke up on Sunday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'to' as a preposition of direction rather than a purpose or negated-purpose pivot, a part-of-speech near-miss for the unigram reading.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She walked to the market to buy bread and cheese for supper yesterday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Ordinary purpose 'to buy' and benefactive 'for supper' with nothing to prevent or watch out for, testing whether any 'to' or 'for' fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He bought a gift for his sister's birthday and hid it in the garden shed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Benefactive 'for' in a completed purchase, a same-token other-sense negative for the look-out 'for'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The open book was lying on the table beside a cup of cold coffee.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Locative 'on' rather than the 'on' of 'keep an eye on', a same-token other-sense negative for the look-out phrase claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The storm destroyed every house on the street and the river flooded the fields.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Danger described without any precaution, the hypothesis's named near-zero class for harm with no avoidance advice.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The team will travel to the capital for the final match next week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Modal 'will travel' plus directional 'to' and purpose 'for' with no precaution, testing bare modality and preposition senses at once.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Are you sure the train leaves at seven in the morning tomorrow?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Epistemic 'sure' in a question, not the recommendation frame of 'make sure', testing whether the bare token fires on its own.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I want a large coffee and a toasted bagel with cream cheese this morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Desire 'want' with a noun object, plus a ' to' token that occurs only as a fragment of 'toasted', testing whether the claimed tokens fire outside any named frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The word avoid appears in the third paragraph of the rental contract.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Metalinguistic mention of the word 'avoid' rather than a precautionary use, a near-miss designed to catch the narrow token-identity reading.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This vaccine prevents infection in about ninety percent of adults who receive it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Descriptive 'prevents' in a medical efficacy claim, prevention stated as fact with no advice or precaution to follow.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rain stopped at noon and the sun finally came out over the hills.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Episodic 'stopped' about the weather, a listed avoidance predicate in a plain past-tense clause with no modal or purpose frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The meeting on Tuesday morning was cancelled because of the heavy snow.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal 'on' in a date phrase with no look-out meaning, another same-token other-sense negative for the look-out 'on'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The recipe calls for two cups of flour and a pinch of salt.
The dough is then left to rise overnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Ordinary sentence-final newline after a full stop rather than a colon-terminated label, which the hypothesis says is much weaker than the label newline it fires on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The children want to build a treehouse in the back garden this summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'want to' with an ordinary verb, testing whether the frame alone fires without any avoidance or prevention predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The board rejected the merger offer after a long debate on Friday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Episodic 'rejected' in a board decision, a listed refusal predicate with no modal, 'want to' or purpose-'to' frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Tie the ladder firmly to the roof rack so as not to lose it on the motorway.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Negated purpose clause 'so as not to lose', the hypothesis's peak frame, in a new road-safety context unlike the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: To avoid missing the last train, we left the party before eleven o'clock.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Purpose-'to' with 'avoid' in a descriptive main clause, which the hypothesis predicts fires but the directive rival does not.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You should avoid touching the exposed wires until the power has been switched off.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Modal 'should avoid' with a precautionary object, one of the hypothesis's core avoidance-in-a-modal frames.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is best to check the tire pressure before a long drive in winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Recommendation frame 'it is best to' before a safety check, a claimed firing frame in a novel automotive context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When you pack for the trip, make sure to bring a warm jacket and gloves.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'make sure to' recommendation carrying the claimed 'sure' token in its precautionary use, a paraphrase holdout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Keep an eye on the children while they swim in the lake this afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Look-out phrase 'keep an eye on', where the hypothesis puts the peak on 'on', in a childcare context with none of the trigger predicates.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Watch out for falling rocks and loose gravel along this section of the trail.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Look-out phrase 'watch out for', where the hypothesis puts the peak on 'for', written as a trail-sign warning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Don't leave the gate open while the sheep are grazing in the field.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Negative imperative 'Don't' in a precaution, testing the hypothesis's claim that the "'t" of don't fires even with no 'to', 'avoid' or 'prevent' present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: To prevent infection, clean the wound twice a day and keep it covered with a bandage.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Purpose-'to' with 'prevent' opening a medical instruction, a claimed pivot in a cross-genre holdout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Equipment:
A whisk, a large mixing bowl, a fine sieve and a wooden spoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Colon-terminated label ending in a newline, the hypothesis's weaker second mode, in a recipe-list context unlike the corpus examples.
